projects.title: Project Net
projects.one_liner: A community map of paracord tension nets in Bellingham, with deliberately fuzzed public locations and a five-step trust ladder for the weavers who hang them.
projects.role: Product, UI and interaction design; built by directing Claude Code
stack: Supabase (Postgres + PostGIS, row-level security, magic links)
highlights: One token system for five risk levels and the weaver levels, Fraunces + Geist, dark mode
Canvas net with spring physics, a map tour, a 'fuzz demo' that explains location privacy, all behind prefers-reduced-motion
Exact coordinates withheld by column grant; public locations fuzzed 50–500 m and re-randomised on save
First overnight autonomous build: 16 commits in one night, with a morning notes file of decisions
projects.live_url_note: Deployed to Vercel; the URL is not in the repo.

image.alt: Project Net mark: three interlocking rings above a short line, cream on dark green

projects.image_note: No screenshots exist in the repo. Capture home, map and about at 1440 and 390 (light + dark) before relying on this card.

projects.title: Nanny-care lead funnel
projects.one_liner: A lead-capture site, QR-coded print flyers, a share card and a confirmation email for a local nanny, with Figma and code kept in step by a copy contract.
projects.role: Brand, UX, Figma design system, print; built by directing Claude Code
highlights: Planned as one unattended overnight run and live the same day, verified by a 12-check table (CORS, honeypot, rate limit, end-to-end submission)
Every Figma text layer is named copy/<id> to match a data-copy anchor in the HTML, so copy edits sweep from Figma to code
Scroll-depth analytics with a household opt-out and a small stats dashboard

image.alt: Nanny-care landing page at desktop width: serif headline, sage and sand palette, credential chips and a 'Get in touch' button

more_images.alt: The same landing page at phone width
Letter-size print flyer with a pull quote and a QR code
Figma color tokens: fifteen named swatches with hex values

projects.privacy: The client is José's partner. Her portrait (OG card, poster, Figma hero) is excluded; the live site shows a photo placeholder.

projects.title: Household finances, as a story
projects.one_liner: A private Python pipeline turns a bank export into a scroll-driven chart story with scenario sliders and a live spreadsheet, and every headline is checked by an adversarial review before anyone reads it.
projects.role: Data analysis, narrative data visualisation; multi-agent analysis directed through a written brief
highlights: Claim-first section titles, written as findings rather than chart labels
A three-level confidence key (✅ / 🔎 / ❓) on every number
Income classified by source text, not the bank's category; an independent pass reconciled the headlines
projects.image_note: No image by design: the dashboard shows real household figures.
projects.privacy: Anonymised. Publish no names, no amounts, no counts and no screenshots of the real dashboard.

projects.title: A fence plan from open city data
projects.one_liner: City GIS layers become a survey-accurate CAD site plan, a letter-size PDF at 1 in = 20 ft, and an interactive fence-budget explorer with a layered SVG plan.
highlights: Parcel, building, water, sewer and storm layers pulled from public GIS and drawn in State Plane coordinates
Fence runs and post layouts generated in code, then dimensioned for a permit-style PDF
A 40-layer SVG plan inside a budget explorer with editable prices and side-by-side options

image.alt: Dark CAD site plan of a residential lot: house footprint in red, fence run with posts every six feet, dimension strings

projects.privacy: It is José's home. Never show the street address; the GIS overview with the address title block is excluded.
